value.title: Multiletter Marton achievability
value.objective: Determine whether finite-letter Marton coding can improve half-skew BSSC achievable sum rates and rigorously characterize structural restrictions on candidate multiletter witnesses.

value.title: Conditional-product no-gain structure
value.summary: Characterize conditional-product Marton architectures that cannot yield multiletter gains and develop decomposition-relative correlation tests for remaining coupled candidates.

value.title: Four padding-correlation tests for a two-letter Marton gain
value.summary:
Accepted statement:

Assume canonical transaction 5ed3f525b9ae7f32c6e1dcbf22ecdb5ae946a4a6 and its exact tuple-law total-correlation residual. For any finite receiver-skew broadcast channel T and any arbitrary finite two-letter Marton law P(W,U,V,X_1,X_2), define A_1=I(Y_2;Y_1,U|W), A_2=I(Y_1;Y_2,U|W), B_1=I(Z_2;Z_1,V|W), B_2=I(Z_1;Z_2,V|W), D=I(U;V|W), and C=(I(Y_1;Y_2|W)+I(Y_1;Y_2)+I(Z_1;Z_2|W)+I(Z_1;Z_2))/2. If this law has Marton value strictly above 2M_T, then A_a+B_b>C+1{a!=b}D for all four (a,b) in {1,2}^2. Hence failure of any one inequality rules out a gain. Adding the crossed tests gives the combined necessary inequality in README equation (12). Applied to the half-skew BSSC, these tests cover every abstract two-letter auxiliary law without assuming an a priori tuple structure. They are necessary only and do not prove additivity, exhibit a gain, or determine capacity.

The combined necessary inequality expressly referenced as README equation (12) is

\[
\begin{aligned}
&I(Y_1;Y_2\mid W)+I(Z_1;Z_2\mid W)
-I(Y_1;Y_2)-I(Z_1;Z_2)\\
&\quad+I(U;Y_2\mid Y_1,W)+I(U;Y_1\mid Y_2,W)\\
&\quad+I(V;Z_2\mid Z_1,W)+I(V;Z_1\mid Z_2,W)
>2I(U;V\mid W).
\end{aligned}
\]

Scope qualifications (verbatim):
- The inequalities are necessary only; they do not prove additivity, exhibit a gaining law, establish sufficiency, or determine capacity.
- The summed crossed condition is weaker than retaining the two crossed inequalities separately.
- The result concerns finite receiver-skew broadcast channels and finite auxiliary alphabets.
- Numerical checker attestations are corroborative only; the universal conclusion rests on the analytic entropy identities.

value.title: Four constant-padding residual proof
value.summary: Proof used to establish the linked accepted claim. For each of the four choices of coordinates, it places the abstract auxiliary U in one coordinate and V in one coordinate while padding the other components by constants. Applying the required exact tuple-law total-correlation residual identifies the resulting residual as A_a+B_b-1{a!=b}D-C. A strict two-letter gain forces each residual to be positive, yielding all four tests. Adding the two crossed tests and applying the displayed chain-rule identities gives the combined necessary inequality. This proof item is limited to the linked necessary conditions and does not establish sufficiency, additivity, a gaining law, or capacity.

placementAudits.rationale: The accepted contribution gives necessary correlation tests for candidate two-letter Marton gains by specializing the existing conditional-product residual framework, so the multiletter Marton achievability program and its conditional-product no-gain thread are the narrowest coherent local objective and thread.
